title: Count and Say

concept.title: Describe the previous term out loud
body: The "count and say" sequence starts with `1`. Each next term describes the previous term by reading it out loud: group equal neighbouring digits and say "how many, which digit". `1` is "one 1" = `11`; `11` is "two 1s" = `21`; `21` is "one 2, one 1" = `1211`; then `111221`.

body.code:
term = "1"
for _ in range(n - 1):
    nxt = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(term):
        j = i
        while j < len(term) and term[j] == term[i]: j += 1
        nxt += str(j - i) + term[i]
        i = j
    term = nxt

body: Splitting a string into runs of equal characters is the same pattern as in string compression. The terms grow quickly (about 30% longer each time), so only small `n` is asked.

statement: The terms of the sequence are: term 1 is `1`, and every next term describes the previous one by counting groups of equal neighbouring digits (the count first, then the digit). The first terms are 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221, 312211. Print term number `n`.

examples.note: Term 3 is 21 ("one 2, one 1"), so term 4 is 1211.

hints: To build the next term, split the current one into runs of equal digits.
For each run write its length and then its digit.

explanation: Each term is produced from the previous one by compressing it into (count, digit) pairs, exactly like run-length encoding.
solution.complexity: Time O(total length of all terms), space O(length of the last term).

code.python:
n = int(input())

term = "1"
for _ in range(n - 1):
    nxt = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(term):
        j = i
        while j < len(term) and term[j] == term[i]:
            j += 1
        nxt.append(str(j - i) + term[i])
        i = j
    term = "".join(nxt)
print(term)
